boundary: Edge of the new August 2026 lava field: coherence loss where fresh lava buried the ground (from the Valle del Leone vents down the floor of the uninhabited Valle del Bove to fronts at ~1,315-1,340 m around Rocca Capra) versus undisturbed ground. Per INGV, no inhabited town was reached by lava. The towns on the lower east flank (Zafferana Etnea) got ash, not lava.

items.title: Lava front at the foot of Rocca Capra, burning broom and pine
items.place: Base of Rocca Capra ridge, lower Valle del Bove, Zafferana Etnea, ~1,340 m
items.what_it_shows: INGV field photo of the advancing lava front at the base of Rocca Capra on 13 Aug 2026. INGV says the most advanced fronts were at ~1,340 m, 'circling the rocky ridge of Rocca Capra and burning and burying broom shrubs and pines'. By 19 Aug a broad front from the 1,900 m vent reached 1,315 m, west of the 13 Aug flow.
items.notes: Rocca Capra summit (OSM peak) is at 37.74156, 15.06799. The lava point is the decorrelated NISAR pixel beside it, not a surveyed front position. ND licence: show the photo unmodified (no crops or overlays on the image itself).

items.title: Rocca Capra ridge: the island the lava flowed around
items.place: Rocca Capra summit, Valle del Bove
items.what_it_shows: The same INGV photo (Figura 8): the ridge stands above the front. This pairs the two sides of the lava edge across a few hundred metres.
items.notes: Location from OSM. Whether lava overtopped any part of the ridge is not stated, only that it surrounded it.

items.title: New vent at Monte Rittmann: cone collapse and small pyroclastic flows
items.place: Monte Rittmann (1986-87 cone), upper Valle del Bove / Valle del Leone, ~2,300-2,360 m
items.what_it_shows: INGV staff on the ground photographed a small pyroclastic flow as a new effusive vent opened at ~2,300 m near Monte Rittmann on 8 Aug 2026. The vent opened on a steep, unstable slope and part of the cone collapsed into the new lava.
items.notes: Point is the OSM Monte Rittmann summit; the vent was 'nei pressi di' (near) it. Low coherence here could also be layover on the steep wall, so do not over-claim it as lava-only.

items.title: Zafferana Etnea: ash, not lava
items.place: Zafferana Etnea town, lower east flank, ~600 m (camera position of the INGV photo)
items.what_it_shows: INGV photo taken from Zafferana Etnea on the morning of 17 Aug 2026: the ash cloud with a veil of falling pyroclastic material over the volcano. The town's experience was ash and airport disruption. Lava stopped ~1,000 m higher, inside the Valle del Bove (INGV: no inhabited town was reached).
items.notes: Point is the OSM centroid of Zafferana Etnea; the exact camera position is unknown. 'No town reached' is stated by etnaunlimited.com (https://www.etnaunlimited.com/post/mount-etna-eruption-august-2026-what-happened), which cites INGV. INGV itself describes the fronts as inside the Valle del Bove.

items.title: Fissure activity on the Voragine, seen from Pizzi Deneri
items.place: Pizzi Deneri (INGV observatory ridge), NE summit area, ~2,800 m
items.what_it_shows: Explosive activity from several vents along the new fissure on the Voragine, 5 Jul 2026, photographed from Pizzi Deneri. This was the precursor episode, before the August flank vents.
items.notes: Weak item: the photo predates the NISAR pair (23 Jul to 16 Aug) and shows the summit, not the lava edge. Include only as a viewpoint or context pin.
